hypothesis: Fixed +/-1% dual-horizon hysteresis reduces whipsaw and trading costs.
observed: 284 held-out chronological daily bars: return 20.1534%, baseline 16.8723%, buy-and-hold 35.0210%; close-marked max drawdown 6.0347%, baseline 7.4021%, buy-and-hold 18.9206%.
trading: 16 fills (8 buys, 8 sells) versus baseline 32 and buy-and-hold 2; 268 valid no-trade days (141 cash, 127 invested) versus baseline 252 and buy-and-hold 282.
costs: Variant fees 1630.3547 and slippage 815.1830; baseline fees 3183.2147 and slippage 1591.6127, on initial equity 100000.
learned: The predeclared buffer halved round trips and improved this baseline's net return by 3.2811 percentage points, with a smaller observed drawdown. It still materially lagged buy-and-hold. Lower fees alone do not establish causality: entry/exit exposures changed too.
failures: No simulation infeasibility or invalid-bar failure. Public SPY acquisition failed; AAPL fallback and shorter evaluation window are disclosed in provenance.
further_validation: Worth independent multi-asset, longer-window validation, without retuning on this sample; not deployment-ready or evidence of competition victory.
